1	# Design — Issue #1801: Retire orch-sequential, harden backend errors, unify kill path
2	
3	## Architectural decision summary
4	
5	**Goal:** Fix stage timeouts silently not applying on the orchestrator route, and close the gaps that enable it: a fallback backend (orch-sequential) that ignores the timeout, a flat 300 s hard-coded deadline that overrides per-stage configuration, and a kill path that only signals individual PIDs rather than process groups.
6	
7	**Context:** Three separate mechanisms interact to make per-stage `timeout_s:` silently ineffective on the orchestrator route. (1) The strategies pass `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300` to `orch_collect` instead of the stage's declared limit. (2) orch-sequential's `orch_collect` ignores `--timeout` entirely, so the 300 s cap never applied to it either. (3) `_runner_dispatch_always_run` reads `router.timeout_s` (the per-call model timeout) as the watchdog bound, not the whole-stage `timeout_s:`. (4) `_orch_local_kill_slot` sends individual-PID signals, leaving child processes alive when the parent ignores TERM. (5) A missing or wrong backend silently falls through to orch-sequential rather than failing fast.
8	
9	**Decision:**
10	1. Retire orch-sequential entirely: delete the plugin directory, the golden, the wiki page; change the `sequential` fallback in `_orch_load_backend` (contract.sh) to `bash-parallel` (the actual system default) — the `sequential` string must not remain anywhere; a config explicitly naming `sequential` or `orch-sequential` ends `misconfigured`.
11	2. Replace the `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300` literal in all three strategies with `template_stage_time_limit "$stage"`, which reads the stage's declared `timeout_s:` (default 900 s). `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT` is no longer read.
12	3. Make a missing backend fatal: `orch_load_backend` no longer falls through to sequential; runner.sh detects the failed load and surfaces it as `misconfigured` naming the backend.
13	4. Fix `_runner_dispatch_always_run` to read `template_stage_time_limit` instead of `router.timeout_s`/`ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT`. Move `timeout_s: 30` (release) and `timeout_s: 120` (persist) from under `router:` to the top-level stage block in both shipped templates so `template_stage_time_limit` finds them. The `always-run-minimal.yaml` fixture template must also have `release.timeout_s: 2` as a direct child of its `release:` block (not under `router:`) — `template_stage_time_limits_load` reads the overlay source file, not the merged template, so the fixture must carry the value explicitly at stage-block indent.
14	5. Route all kills through `zbuild_pg_kill`/`zbuild_pid_kill`: source `proc-group.sh` in `local_engine.sh`; replace the bare `kill` calls in `_orch_local_kill_slot` and the watchdog in `_runner_dispatch_always_run` with the shared helper.

# Design — Issue #1801: Retire orch-sequential, harden backend errors, unify kill path

## Architectural decision summary

**Goal:** Fix stage timeouts silently not applying on the orchestrator route, and close the gaps that enable it: a fallback backend (orch-sequential) that ignores the timeout, a flat 300 s hard-coded deadline that overrides per-stage configuration, and a kill path that only signals individual PIDs rather than process groups.

**Context:** Three separate mechanisms interact to make per-stage `timeout_s:` silently ineffective on the orchestrator route. (1) The strategies pass `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300` to `orch_collect` instead of the stage's declared limit. (2) orch-sequential's `orch_collect` ignores `--timeout` entirely, so the 300 s cap never applied to it either. (3) `_runner_dispatch_always_run` reads `router.timeout_s` (the per-call model timeout) as the watchdog bound, not the whole-stage `timeout_s:`. (4) `_orch_local_kill_slot` sends individual-PID signals, leaving child processes alive when the parent ignores TERM. (5) A missing or wrong backend silently falls through to orch-sequential rather than failing fast.

**Decision:**
1. Retire orch-sequential entirely: delete the plugin directory, the golden, the wiki page; change the `sequential` fallback in `_orch_load_backend` (contract.sh) to `bash-parallel` (the actual system default) — the `sequential` string must not remain anywhere; a config explicitly naming `sequential` or `orch-sequential` ends `misconfigured`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: #1831 — an `always_run:` stage runs on EVERY exit path.
#
# This is the assertion the attribute exists for. A mechanism that fires on four
# of five exit paths is #1878's defect wearing a new name ("the snapshot was
# never called"), so each path gets its own case and names itself on failure —
# a single parameterised assertion would report "one of five" and leave the
# operator to find which.
#
# Paths covered: rc=0, rc=1, a stage killed by SIGINT (rc=130 + the recorded
# abort word), SIGTERM to the runner, and a release hook that hangs past its
# own timeout_s.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "always_run dispatches on every exit path (#1831)"
setup_test_env "zb-always-run-exit"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo always-run-overlay)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" always-run-minimal

# The always-run plugin, bound by ROLE (not by directory — that coupling is
# what #1831 removes). It touches a marker so "did it run?" is a file test
# rather than an inference from an event that might not be emitted.
mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran"
RELEASE_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-entered"
_arm_release() {
    # Two markers, not one. ENTERED is written before the optional sleep,
    # RAN after it. With a single completion marker, "the watchdog killed a
    # hanging hook" and "the hook was never dispatched at all" are the same
    # observation — and SPEC-5 passed for that wrong reason during development,
    # before the dispatch worked at all.
    # $1 = optional `sleep N` injected between the two, for the watchdog case.
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_ENTERED}"
    ${1:-:}
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    return 0
}
PLUG
}

# The stage announces that it is RUNNING (#2029). `pipeline-state.json` appears
# during startup, long before any stage is dispatched, so waiting on it and then
# sleeping a second is not "the stage has started" — it is a guess that happens to
# hold on an idle machine.
#
# On a loaded one it does not, and SPEC-4 then SIGTERMs a runner still setting up
# its worktree: no stage has run, no release hook is armed, no marker is written,
# and the assertion reports a missing file with no hint that the run never got
# that far. Observed directly — `wait` returned in 0s, the hook-entered marker was
# absent, and the runner's last line was "Working in the run's worktree".
#
# `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` already does this correctly with
# BUILD_STARTED; this is the same idea. The marker can only appear once the stage
# is genuinely executing, so load can only delay it, never fake it.
# #1850: the stage writes the v2 result its manifest (mock_plugin_factory's)
# promises — pass on rc 0, error/broken otherwise — so a run that should succeed
# is not failed for leaving no readable result.
_arm_outcome() {
    local _o=pass
    [[ "${2:-0}" -ne 0 ]] && _o=broken
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "\${STAGE_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    ${1:-:}
    $(mock_result_line outcome "$_o")
    return ${2:-0}
}
PLUG
}

# Each case gets its own state dir: a stale marker or state file from a prior
# case would make a later one pass for the wrong reason.
_run_case() {
    local name="$1" rc_want_set="$2"
    rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-$name"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    set +e
    ( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
        --goal "always-run $name" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name.out" 2>&1
    _CASE_RC=$?
    set -e
    [[ "$rc_want_set" == "skip" ]] || true
}

# ─── [SPEC-1][change] rc=0 — the ordinary success path ──────────────────────
print_test_section "[SPEC-1][change] release runs when the pipeline succeeds"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 0
_run_case "rc0" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-1] release ran on rc=0" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-2][change] rc=1 — a failed run still frees its resources ─────────
# The failing path is the one that matters most: a run that died is exactly the
# run holding process groups and locks nobody else will clean up.
print_test_section "[SPEC-2][change] release runs when a stage fails"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "" 1
_run_case "rc1" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-2] release ran on a non-zero stage rc" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-3][change] the SIGINT path ─────────────────────────────────────
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025): the SIGINT path is the recorded abort word, not
# rc=130 — a bare 130 from a stage is just a failed stage now. So the stage
# does what a Ctrl-C does to the process group: the sentinel is armed (empty =
# sigint) and the child dies with 130. The run must end on the abort path —
# exit 1, status interrupted — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2.
print_test_section "[SPEC-3][change] release runs on the SIGINT path (abort word sigint)"
_arm_release
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # expanded by the stage at run time, not here
_arm_outcome ': > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/.abort.signal"' 130
_run_case "rc130" skip
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-3] release ran on the SIGINT path" "$RELEASE_MARKER"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] the run took the abort path: exit 1 (not 130), status interrupted" \
    "1 interrupted" "$_CASE_RC $(jq -r '.status // "MISSING"' "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-rc130/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"

# ─── [SPEC-4][change] SIGTERM delivered to the runner itself ───────────────
# Distinct from SPEC-3: there the stage returned a code, here the signal is
# delivered to the runner process while a stage is still executing. #1759's
# re-armed INT/TERM traps are what give this path somewhere to hang off.
print_test_section "[SPEC-4][change] release runs when the runner is SIGTERMed mid-stage"
_arm_release; _arm_outcome "sleep 30" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-sigterm"
export STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-started-sigterm"
rm -f "$STAGE_STARTED"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run sigterm" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>&1 &
_runner_pid=$!
# Wait for the run to actually reach the stage before signalling — signalling a
# runner still in startup would prove nothing about the exit path.
#
# #2029: this used to wait for `pipeline-state.json` and then sleep 1. That file
# is written during STARTUP, so the wait proved nothing and the sleep was the only
# real margin. Under load it was not enough and the signal landed mid-startup.
# STAGE_STARTED is written by the stage itself, so it cannot be reached early.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" && $_waited -lt 300 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done
if [[ ! -f "$STAGE_STARTED" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage started before the signal was sent" \
        "STAGE_STARTED never appeared in 60s — the run never reached a stage, so the exit path was never exercised"
fi
_spec4_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
_spec4_wait_s=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec4_t0 ))
# The trap runs in the dying process; give it a moment to land the marker.
_waited=0
while [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" && $_waited -lt 50 ]]; do
    sleep 0.2; _waited=$(( _waited + 1 ))
done

# #2029: say WHAT WAS SEEN, not merely that the file is absent.
#
# This assertion has failed intermittently on CI for as long as it has existed,
# and it could never be diagnosed because "file not found" is the same output
# whether the runner ignored the signal, died before its trap, ran teardown into
# a different path, or simply had not finished yet. Three separate mechanisms
# were proposed for it and all three were disproven.
#
# The sibling assertion in runner-release-exit-paths prints the marker it read,
# and that one line is what let #2046 identify its cause in minutes after days of
# guessing. This is that lesson applied here: the next occurrence explains itself
# instead of starting another hunt.
if [[ ! -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    {
        printf '  DIAGNOSTIC [SPEC-4]: release marker absent after %ss of polling\n' "$(( _waited * 2 / 10 ))"
        printf '    wait on the runner returned after: %ss\n' "$_spec4_wait_s"
        printf '    runner pid %s still alive: %s\n' "$_runner_pid" \
            "$(kill -0 "$_runner_pid" 2>/dev/null && echo YES || echo no)"
        printf '    release hook ENTERED marker: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -f "$RELEASE_ENTERED" ]] && echo present || echo absent)"
        printf '    state dir: %s\n' \
            "$([[ -d "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" ]] && (cd "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" && printf '%s ' * 2>/dev/null) || echo '<missing>')"
        printf '    runner output (last 5 lines):\n'
        tail -5 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/sigterm.out" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/      /' || printf '      <no output>\n'
    } >&2
fi
# RELEASE_ENTERED separates "the hook never started" from "it started and did not
# finish" — the single most useful split, and the one the bare check cannot make.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-4] release ran after SIGTERM to the runner" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [SPEC-5][guard] a hanging release cannot hang the exit ────────────────
# The stage declares timeout_s: 2. A hook that blocks past it must be killed and
# the exit must continue — otherwise Ctrl-C becomes a lockup, which is the exact
# class of bug an EXIT-trap dispatch exists to avoid. Asserting the WALL CLOCK
# rather than the marker: the marker would also be absent if release never ran
# at all, so it cannot distinguish "bounded" from "broken".
print_test_section "[SPEC-5][guard] a release hook that hangs is bounded by its timeout_s"
_arm_release "sleep 60"; _arm_outcome "" 0
rm -f "$RELEASE_MARKER" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-hang"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-minimal \
    --goal "always-run hang" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/hang.out" 2>&1
set -e
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# 45s is generous against a 2s bound plus runner startup; the assertion is
# "bounded at all", not a tight budget — a tight one would flake under a loaded
# parallel pool (the #991 lesson).
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 45 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook did not hold the exit (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] a 60s release hook held the exit" "elapsed=${_elapsed}s"
fi
# These two together are what make the case meaningful: the hook WAS entered
# (so the bound is what stopped it) and did NOT complete (so it was actually
# killed). Either alone is satisfied by a dispatch that never happened.
assert_file_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was actually dispatched" "$RELEASE_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[SPEC-5] the hanging hook was killed before completing" "$RELEASE_MARKER"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-5]: persist always_run stage bounded by timeout_s: (not 120s) ─
# _runner_dispatch_always_run must use template_stage_time_limit (top-level
# timeout_s:) instead of ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s.
# The fixture template sets persist.timeout_s: 4 (new code reads) and
# persist.router.timeout_s: 120 (old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT / router.timeout_s).
# A blocking persist hook must be killed in ~4s, NOT ~120s.
# FAILS on old code (elapsed ~120s > 20), PASSES on new code (elapsed ~4s < 20).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog uses timeout_s: not router.timeout_s: 120"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: persist
name: Persist Stub Spec5
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: persist_run
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  role: persist
MF
_SPEC5P_ENTERED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p-entered"
_SPEC5P_DONE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p-done"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
persist_run() {
    : > "${_SPEC5P_ENTERED}"
    sleep 120
    : > "${_SPEC5P_DONE}"
    return 0
}
PLUG

_spec5p_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "always-run-spec5p")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5p_repo" always-run-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5p_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5p_repo/.zbuild/templates/always-run-spec5p.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: always-run-spec5p
extends: always-run-minimal
always_run:
  - release
  - persist
persist:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  timeout_s: 4
  router:
    timeout_s: 120
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
YAML
_arm_outcome "" 0
_arm_release
rm -f "$_SPEC5P_ENTERED" "$_SPEC5P_DONE"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-spec5p"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/spec5p-events.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
_spec5p_t0=$(date +%s)
set +e
( cd "$_spec5p_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template always-run-spec5p \
    --goal "spec5-persist" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec5p.out" 2>&1
set -e
_spec5p_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _spec5p_t0 ))
if [[ "$_spec5p_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog bounds at timeout_s: 4 (exited in ${_spec5p_elapsed}s; old code: router.timeout_s: 120)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist always_run watchdog must use timeout_s: 4" \
        "runner took ${_spec5p_elapsed}s; expected < 20s (timeout_s: 4); old code reads router.timeout_s: 120 → ~120s"
fi
assert_file_exists "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist hook was entered (always_run persist stage dispatched)" "$_SPEC5P_ENTERED"
assert_file_not_exists "[#1801/SPEC-5] persist hook killed before completing (bounded by timeout_s: 4, not 120s)" "$_SPEC5P_DONE"

# ─── [SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable always-run role is LOUD ───────────────
# The code this replaces did `[[ -d "$_td_dir" ]] || return 0` — a missing
# plugin was a silent no-op. An always-run stage that cannot be resolved has not
# run, and the operator must be able to see that rather than infer it from a
# missing effect.
print_test_section "[SPEC-6][guard] an unresolvable role emits an event instead of failing silently"
_arm_outcome "" 0

rm -rf "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events/unresolved.jsonl"

set +e

    --goal "always-run unresolved" ) >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unresolved.out" 2>&1
_unres_rc=$?
set -e
assert_event_emitted "[SPEC-6] stage.always_run.unresolved is emitted" \
    "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" "stage.always_run.unresolved"
# And it must not change the run's fate — an always-run stage never decides the
# verdict, including when it could not be found.
assert_eq "[SPEC-6] an unresolvable always-run stage does not fail the run" "0" "$_unres_rc"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
3	# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
4	# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
5	#
6	# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
7	# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
8	# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
9	#
10	# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
11	# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
12	# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
13	# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
14	# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
15	# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
16	# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
17	# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in

448	for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
449	    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
450	    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
451	done
452	_alive=1
453	# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
454	if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
455	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
456	fi
457	if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
458	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
459	elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
460	    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
461	    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
462	else
463	    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
464	fi
465	
466	# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
467	# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
468	# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
469	# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
470	# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
471	# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
472	# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
473	print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
474	wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
475	CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
476	_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
477	if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
478	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
479	else
480	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
481	        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
482	fi
483	
484	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
485	# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
486	# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
487	# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
488	if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
489	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
490	else
491	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
492	        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
493	fi
494	
495	# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
496	# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
497	# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
498	# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
499	# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
500	# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
501	if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
502	    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
503	else
504	    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
505	        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
506	fi
507	
508	cleanup_test_env
509	print_test_results
510	exit $((FAIL > 0))
511

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#
# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
    (
        _prep "$1"
        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
        _t0=$(date +%s)
        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
    ) &
}
_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!
_start_blocking blocking-ignore-term BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM; _SPEC6B_PID=$!
_SPEC6_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking"
_SPEC6B_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking-ignore-term"

# [#1801/SPEC-5]: blocking run with timeout_s: 5 for release (top-level, read
# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).
_spec5_bound_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5-bound")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: resume-spec5-bound
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: 5
YAML
_start_blocking spec5-bound BLOCK_CLEANUP resume-spec5-bound; _SPEC5_BOUND_PID=$!
_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-spec5-bound"

# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
_prep success
export BUILD_RC=0
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# SPEC-6/6b run alongside this case; if it fails, say what the runner said.
[[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] || tail -20 "$CASE_DIR/out" >&2
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test

# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
_prep nonzero
export BUILD_RC=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
fi
_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build

# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
_prep sigint
export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
else
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
fi
for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
_build_pid="$(head -n 1 "$BUILD_STARTED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# ADR-054 §7: the runner acts on the signal while the stage is still running.
# Build holds for 30s; a runner that waits for it to return took 30s+ here.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 15 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage" "took ${_elapsed}s; build holds 30s"
fi
if [[ -n "$_build_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run" "build pid $_build_pid still alive"
    kill -KILL "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run"
fi
# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build

# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
#
# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
# runs could never reproduce.
#
# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
_prep timeout
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
_tbin=""
if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # [#1801/SPEC-5]: #2029: the force-kill grace is DERIVED from the engine's own
    # teardown budget, not guessed.
    #
    # After #1801 the engine bounds each always-run stage by template_stage_time_limit
    # (top-level `timeout_s:` in the stage block), NOT by router.timeout_s or
    # ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT. The template below pins timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT
    # for release so the worst case is knowable and the grace derives from it.
    # This case relies on its hooks returning promptly rather than on the bound —
    # the grace is purely a safety net so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the
    # suite. Three stages release on this path, so an unpinned run could spend far
    # longer tidying up than the 3s literal that used to sit here.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    # Create a repo with a template that has timeout_s: _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT for
    # release (top-level, read by template_stage_time_limit after #1801).
    _spec5_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5")"
    install_template_overlay "$_spec5_repo" resume-minimal
    if [[ -d "$_spec5_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
       ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_repo/.git/info/exclude"
    fi
    cat > "$_spec5_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-timeout-bounded.yaml" <<YAMLEOF
id: resume-timeout-bounded
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: ${_SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT}
YAMLEOF
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-timeout-bounded --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$_spec5_repo" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.

270	# reported, never fatal.
271	_runner_push_work_branch() {
272	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
273	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
274	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
275	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
276	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
277	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
278	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
279	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
280	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
281	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
282	    local _err
283	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
284	        return 0
285	    fi
286	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
287	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
288	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
289	    return 0
290	}

292	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
293	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
294	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
295	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
296	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
297	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
298	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
299	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
300	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
301	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
302	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
303	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
304	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
305	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
306	        reattached)
307	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
308	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
309	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
310	        diverged)
311	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
312	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
313	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
314	    esac
315	    return 0
316	}

318	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
319	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
320	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
321	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
322	# never blocks a run.
323	#
324	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
325	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
326	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
327	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
328	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
329	# item 1 of #1807.
330	#
331	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
332	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
333	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
334	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
335	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
336	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
337	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
338	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
339	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
340	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
341	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
342	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
343	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
344	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
345	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
346	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
347	    # push had nothing to send.
348	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
349	
350	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
351	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
352	        saved)
353	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
354	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
355	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
356	            ;;
357	        failed)
358	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
359	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
360	            # no channel to surface on.
361	            #
362	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
363	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
364	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
365	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
366	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
367	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
368	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
370	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
371	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
372	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
373	            fi
374	            ;;
375	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
376	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
377	        *) : ;;
378	    esac
379	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
380	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
381	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
382	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
383	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
384	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
385	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
386	    local _leak=""
387	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
388	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
389	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
390	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
391	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
392	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
393	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
394	        return 0
395	    fi
396	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
397	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
398	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
399	    fi
400	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
401	    return 0
402	}

406	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
407	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.

410	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
411	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
412	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
413	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
414	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).

417	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
418	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
419	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
420	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
421	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
422	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
423	_runner_now_ms() {
424	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
425	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
426	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
427	        return 0
428	    fi
429	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
430	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
431	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
432	        return 0
433	    fi
434	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"

437	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
438	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
439	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
440	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
441	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
442	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
443	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
444	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
445	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
446	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
447	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
448	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
449	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
450	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
451	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
452	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
453	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
454	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
455	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
456	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
457	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
458	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
459	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
460	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
461	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
462	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
463	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
464	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
465	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
466	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
467	    return 0
468	}

470	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
471	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
472	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
473	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
474	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
475	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
476	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
477	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
478	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
479	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
480	        local i
481	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
482	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
483	            sleep 0.1
484	        done
485	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
486	    fi
487	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    return 0
489	}

491	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
492	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
493	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
494	_runner_now_short() {
495	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
496	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
497	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
498	        return 0
499	    fi
500	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
501	    local out
502	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
503	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
504	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
505	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
506	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
507	    printf '%s' "$out"
508	}

510	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
511	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
512	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
513	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
514	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
515	_runner_duration_token() {
516	    local stage="$1"
517	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
518	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
519	        printf '?s'
520	        return 0
521	    fi
522	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
523	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
524	        printf '?s'
525	        return 0
526	    fi
527	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
528	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
529	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
530	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
531	    else
532	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
533	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
534	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
535	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
536	    fi
537	}

573	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
574	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
575	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
576	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
577	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
578	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
579	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
580	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
581	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
582	_runner_record_report() {
583	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
584	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
585	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
586	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
587	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
588	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
589	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
590	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
591	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
592	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
593	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
594	        sleep 0.05
595	    done
596	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
597	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
598	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
599	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
600	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
601	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
602	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
603	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
604	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
605	    else
606	        rm -f "$tmp"
607	    fi
608	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
609	    return 0
610	}

612	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
613	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
614	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
615	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
616	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
617	#
618	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
619	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
620	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
621	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
622	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
623	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
624	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
625	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
626	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
627	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
628	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
629	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
630	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
631	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
632	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
633	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
634	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
635	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
636	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
637	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
638	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
639	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
640	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
645	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
646	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
647	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
648	        return 1
649	    fi
650	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
651	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
652	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
653	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
654	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
655	    #
656	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
657	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
658	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
659	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
660	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
661	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
662	    #
663	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
664	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
665	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
666	    #
667	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
668	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
669	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
670	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
671	    fi
672	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
673	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
674	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
675	    # an unchanged tree.
676	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
677	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
678	    fi
679	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"

698	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
699	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
700	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
701	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
702	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
703	#
704	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
705	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
706	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
707	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
708	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
709	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
710	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
711	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
712	#
713	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
714	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
715	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
716	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
717	#
718	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
719	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
720	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
721	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
722	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
723	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
724	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
725	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
726	_runner_template_personas() {
727	    awk '
728	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
729	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
730	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
731	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
732	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
733	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
734	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
735	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
736	        }
737	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
738	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
739	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
740	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
741	        }
742	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
743	}

745	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
746	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
747	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
748	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
749	    case "$mode" in
750	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
751	        *) mode="warn" ;;
752	    esac
753	
754	    # off = complete no-op, no output
755	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
756	
757	    local -a violations=()
758	    local fail_count=0
759	
760	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
761	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
762	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
763	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
764	    fi
765	
766	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
767	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
768	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
769	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
770	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
771	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
772	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
773	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
774	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
775	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
776	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
777	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
778	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
779	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
780	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
781	    fi
782	
783	    # No violations → clean
784	    [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]] && return 0
785	
786	    # Render all violations in a single block (render-all-at-once pattern).
787	    # #1826 moved the loop itself into _inputs_render_violations so the
788	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
789	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
790	    _inputs_render_violations \
791	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
792	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
793	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
794	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
795	        "${violations[@]}"
796	
797	    # Emit event (best-effort)
798	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
800	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
801	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
802	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
803	    fi
804	
805	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
806	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
807	        return 0
808	    fi
809	
810	    # enforce: fail-closed
811	    return 1
812	}

837	# ─── _runner_pipeline_duration_token (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
838	# Parallel to _runner_duration_token but for the pipeline-wide window. No stage
839	# argument — reads _RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS directly. Returns "?s" on cache
840	# miss so the banner still renders during very-early failures.
841	_runner_pipeline_duration_token() {
842	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"
843	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
844	        printf '?s'
845	        return 0
846	    fi
847	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
848	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
849	        printf '?s'
850	        return 0
851	    fi
852	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
853	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
854	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
855	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
856	    else
857	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
858	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
859	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
860	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
861	    fi

902	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
903	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
904	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
905	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
906	#
907	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
908	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
909	#
910	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
911	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
912	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
913	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
914	#
915	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
916	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
917	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
918	# against banner-write failures.
919	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
920	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
921	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
922	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
923	_runner_restore_stderr() {
924	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
925	    return 0
926	}

928	_render_pipeline_end() {
929	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
930	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
931	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
932	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
933	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
934	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
935	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
936	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
937	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
938	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
939	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
940	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
941	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
942	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
943	    # (#1156)
944	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
945	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
946	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
947	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
948	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
949	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
950	
951	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
952	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
953	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
954	    local word
955	    case "$status" in
956	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
957	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
958	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
959	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
960	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
961	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
962	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
963	    esac
964	
965	    local label=" pipeline.end "
966	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
967	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
968	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
969	
970	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
971	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
972	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
973	
974	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
975	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
976	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
977	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
978	        local bar
979	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
980	        bar="${bar// /═}"
981	        {
982	            printf '\n'
983	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
984	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
985	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
986	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
987	        } >&2
988	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
989	        return 0
990	    fi
991	
992	    local lbar rbar
993	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
994	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
995	    {
996	        printf '\n'
997	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
998	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
999	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1000	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
1001	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
1002	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
1003	    } >&2
1004	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
1005	}
